taskVersion.name: deadline-math-hard-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Exploratory hard set, reasoning allowed. Convert deadlines to the reader's local time: relative dates, durations across a clock change, Unix and ISO timestamps, described dates, a traveling reader. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to find the deadline in Madrid local time.

The deadline is Friday, October 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM PT.

**Step 1: Determine PT offset.**
October 30, 2026 is still before the first Sunday in November (November 1, 2026), so Pacific Time is PDT (UTC-7).

11:59 PM PDT = 23:59 PDT = 23:59 + 7:00 = 06:59 UTC on October 31, 2026.

**Step 2: Determine Madrid offset.**
Madrid uses CET/CEST. In 2026, European clocks fall back the last Sunday of October, which is October 25, 2026. So by October 31, Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).

06:59 UTC on October 31 → 07:59 CET on October 31, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to find when "this coming Monday" after Friday, October 30, 2026 is, and convert from Los Angeles time to Madrid time.

**Step 1: Find the date of "this coming Monday"**
Friday, October 30, 2026 → the coming Monday is November 2, 2026.

**Step 2: Determine time zones on November 2, 2026**

- **Los Angeles (Pacific Time):** Daylight Saving Time ends on the first Sunday of November in the US. November 1, 2026 is a Sunday, so DST ends that day. By Monday, November 2, Los Angeles is on PST (UTC-8).

- **Madrid (CET/CEST):** Europe's DST ends on the last Sunday of October. October 25, 2026 is the last Sunday of October. So by November 2, Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).

**Step 3: Convert**
Monday, November 2, 2026, 10:00 AM PST = 10:00 AM UTC-8 = 18:00 UTC = 19:00 UTC+1 (Madrid CET).

So the deadline is Monday, November 2, 2026 at 19:00 Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to determine when the hackathon ends, starting from Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time, lasting exactly 48 hours.

First, let me consider the time zone situation. Madrid uses CET (UTC+1) in winter and CEST (UTC+2) in summer. The clocks fall back on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, the last Sunday of October is October 25, 2026. Clocks go back from 3:00 CEST to 2:00 CET on that date.

So the hackathon starts on Saturday, October 24 at 18:00 CEST (UTC+2).

Start time in UTC: October 24 at 16:00 UTC.

Adding 48 hours: October 26 at 16:00 UTC.

Now I need to convert back to Madrid local time. Since the clocks fell back on October 25 at 3:00 AM (to 2:00 AM), by October 26 Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).

So October 26 at 16:00 UTC = October 26 at 17:00 CET (Madrid local time).

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 17:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert the deadline from PT to Madrid local time.

**Step 1: Find the deadline in PT.**
The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT. Adding 72 hours (3 days) gives: **October 29, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT**.

**Step 2: Determine which PT offset applies.**
October 29, 2026 is before the first Sunday in November (November 1, 2026), so the US is still on Pacific Daylight Time (PDT = UTC−7).

So the deadline is October 29, 2026 at 10:00 AM PDT = 17:00 UTC.

**Step 3: Determine Madrid's offset.**
Madrid follows CET/CEST. Clocks fall back the last Sunday of October, which in 2026 is October 25. So by October 29, Madrid is on CET = UTC+1.

**Step 4: Convert.**
17:00 UTC = 18:00 CET (UTC+1).

The deadline in Madrid is October 29, 2026 at 18:00.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to find when results are announced in Madrid local time.

**Step 1: Determine when submissions close in ET.**
October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET (Eastern Time).

**Step 2: Add 36 hours to get the announcement time in ET.**
- October 31, 11:59 PM + 24 hours = November 1, 11:59 PM ET
- November 1, 11:59 PM + 12 hours = November 2, 11:59 AM ET

So the announcement is November 2, 2026 at 11:59 AM ET.

**Step 3: Convert from ET to Madrid time.**
I need to determine the UTC offset for both zones on November 2, 2026.

- **US Eastern Time**: Daylight Saving Time ends on the first Sunday of November 2026, which is November 1, 2026. So on November 2, the US is on EST (UTC-5).
- **Madrid (CET/CEST)**: Europe switches back to standard time on the last Sunday of October 2026, which is October 25, 2026. So on November 2, Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).

The difference between EST (UTC-5) and CET (UTC+1) is 6 hours. Madrid is 6 hours ahead of EST.

**Step 4: Convert.**
November 2, 2026 at 11:59 AM EST + 6 hours = November 2, 2026 at 5:59 PM CET.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 17:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert Unix timestamp 1791788340 to Tokyo local time (JST, UTC+9).

Let me work this out step by step.

Starting from Unix epoch (January 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC):

1791788340 seconds ÷ 86400 seconds/day = 20738.75 days (approximately)

Let me use a more structured approach:

- 1791788340 seconds
- Let me estimate the year: 
  - Through 2025: 55 years. From 1970 to 2025 is ~20089 days (accounting for leap years: 55×365 + 13 leap years = 20075 + 13 = 20088 days) → 20088 × 86400 = 1,735,603,200
  - Remaining: 1,791,788,340 - 1,735,603,200 = 56,185,140 seconds
  - 56,185,140 / 86400 = 650.29 days from Jan 1, 2025
  - 650 days from Jan 1, 2025:
    - 2025: 365 days → leaves 285 days into 2026
    - 285 days into 2026: Jan(31) + Feb(28) + Mar(31) + Apr(30) + May(31) + Jun(30) + Jul(31) + Aug(31) + Sep(30) = 273 days through Sep 30
    - 285 - 273 = 12 → October 12, 2026
  - Remaining seconds: 0.29 × 86400 ≈ 25,140 seconds
  - 25,140 / 3600 = 6.983 hours ≈ 6 hours 59 minutes UTC

So the timestamp is approximately October 12, 2026 at 06:59 UTC.

Let me verify more precisely:
- 56,185,140 - 650×86400 = 56,185,140 - 56,160,000 = 25,140 seconds
- 25,140 / 3600 = 6 hours, remainder 1540 seconds
- Wait, 6 × 3600 = 21,600. 25,140 - 21,600 = 3,540 seconds
- 3,540 / 60 = 59 minutes

So UTC: 2026-10-12 06:59

Tokyo time (UTC+9): 2026-10-12 15:59

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 15:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z (UTC) to Madrid local time.

Madrid is in the CET/CEST time zone. I need to determine whether daylight saving time (CEST, UTC+2) or standard time (CET, UTC+1) applies at that moment.

In the EU, clocks fall back on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, the last Sunday of October is October 25. The clocks fall back at 3:00 AM local CEST time, which corresponds to 1:00 AM UTC.

So at 2026-10-25T01:00:00Z, clocks go from CEST (UTC+2) back to CET (UTC+1).

Since the deadline is at 02:30 UTC, which is after the 01:00 UTC switchover, Madrid is now on CET (UTC+1).

2026-10-25T02:30:00Z + 1 hour = 2026-10-25T03:30 local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 03:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to find the last Sunday of October 2026 and convert 11:59 PM Pacific Time to Madrid local time.

**Last Sunday of October 2026:**
October 2026 starts on a Thursday. Let me find the Sundays:
- Oct 4, 11, 18, 25 are Sundays.
The last Sunday of October 2026 is **October 25, 2026**.

**Time zone conversion:**

Now, here's the key detail: the last Sunday of October is exactly when Europe changes clocks (fall back), and I need to check what's happening in both time zones.

- **Pacific Time:** Daylight Saving Time in the US doesn't end until the first Sunday of November (November 1, 2026). So on October 25, 2026, Pacific Time is still PDT (UTC-7).

- **Madrid (Europe/Madrid):** Europe's DST ends on the last Sunday of October. Clocks fall back at 3:00 AM local time (which is 1:00 AM UTC) on October 25, 2026. So after that point, Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).

**The deadline is 11:59 PM PDT on October 25, 2026.**
- 11:59 PM PDT = 23:59 UTC-7 = 06:59 UTC on October 26, 2026.
- Madrid is on CET (UTC+1) by then, so: 06:59 UTC + 1 = 07:59 on October 26, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to figure out when the US ends daylight saving time in 2026 and convert the deadline to Lima, Peru time.

**Step 1: When does the US end daylight saving time in 2026?**

The US ends daylight saving time on the first Sunday in November. In 2026, November 1 is a Sunday. So DST ends on **November 1, 2026**.

**Step 2: What is Eastern Time at that moment?**

The deadline says "12:00 noon Eastern Time." On the day DST ends, clocks fall back at 2:00 AM. So by noon, the US has already fallen back to Eastern Standard Time (EST), which is UTC-5.

So 12:00 noon EST = 12:00 noon UTC-5 = 17:00 UTC.

**Step 3: Convert to Lima, Peru time.**

Lima, Peru uses PET (Peru Time), which is UTC-5 year-round. Peru does not observe daylight saving time.

So Lima is also UTC-5 at that time.

17:00 UTC = 12:00 noon UTC-5 (Lima time).

The deadline in Lima is 12:00 noon on November 1, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

**Reasoning:**

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) corresponds to UTC-12, the last time zone on Earth.

Tokyo is in JST, which is UTC+9.

The difference between UTC-12 and UTC+9 is 21 hours. So Tokyo is 21 hours ahead of AoE.

December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE = January 1, 2027, 00:00 UTC-12.

Converting to UTC: January 1, 2027, 00:00 + 12 hours = January 1, 2027, 12:00 UTC.

Converting to JST (UTC+9): January 1, 2027, 12:00 + 9 hours = January 1, 2027, 21:00 JST.

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026 to New York time.

**Sydney time on October 5, 2026:**
October 5 falls during Australian Daylight Saving Time (AEDT), which is UTC+11.

So 5:00 PM AEDT = 17:00 AEDT = 06:00 UTC on October 5, 2026.

**New York time on October 5, 2026:**
October 5 is before the first Sunday in November, so New York is still on Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), which is UTC-4.

06:00 UTC = 06:00 - 4:00 = 02:00 EDT on October 5, 2026.

So the deadline is 2:00 AM New York time on October 5, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
